newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Smart car exec sees full output start in November.
newsitem.headline: Smart car exec sees full output start in November.

text.p: A top executive at Micro Computer Car (MCC), a joint venture between Daimler-Benz AG and SMH Group, said the carmaker will begin full test production in April of the new "Smart" car and full production in November.
Johann Tomforde, in charge of development at Smart, told Reuters in an interview at the Geneva car show that the carmaker still intended to launch the car in early 1998.
"The production facility is pretty much completed and we will begin the testing phase in April and full production in November," Tomforde said.
The Smart car is a two-seat microcompact vehicle being developed by Mercedes and SMH, the parent company of watchmaker Swatch. It will be built at a factory in France.
Annual production capacity has been set at 200,000 vehicles but Tomforde declined to predict the current production forecasts for the first year of sales.
Tomforde said the Smart car's introduction will focus on "core markets" in Europe and that the carmaker had no immediate plans for a rollout in the United States.

Auto industry trade publications have said Smart was planning to introduce the vehicle into the U.S. about two months after its European launch and may consider building the car at Mercedes' new factory in Alabama.
"We are going to concentrate on the core of Europe and will then build up our presence in the rest of Europe," he said.
"America is not a top priority right now," he said. "We want to put our full concentration on Europe and not disturb the process."

Tomforde also said Mercedes, which owns 51 percent of the venture, has decided not to put its trademark "star" on the vehicle, which is only 2.5 meters long and will have a three-cylinder engine. The car can be built in 4.5 hours.

But he reaffirmed Mercedes' support for the project and continuing production help from the Stuttgart carmaker, where the Smart car is treated as a separate operating division from Mercedes passenger vehicles.
"This car will be called the Smart car but the heart of this car is certainly from Mercedes," he said.

Mercedes is hoping to tap into the expanding small-car market with the Smart car, which will cost 15,000 to 20,000 marks, as well as its new A class vehicle, which was unveiled this week at the Geneva car show.
Tomforde said the market for vehicles costing under 30,000 marks in Europe accounts for more than 60 percent of the cars sold in Europe, a market where Mercedes has been lacking.
